comparison: Both strongly support V2R activation of Gαs and Gαq/11 at plasma membrane and endosomes. OpenEval emphasizes multiple complementary approaches (mG proteins, confocal microscopy, DAG production) with appropriate controls. Peer reviewers accept findings without challenge, noting 'state of the art biosensor-based approaches' and that the study 'demonstrates the possibility that Gq might also be activated by the V2 receptor.'

Both support Gαq/11-mediated DAG production findings. OpenEval highlights biosensor approaches with pharmacological controls (YM254890) and PKC activation validation. Peer review accepts these findings as part of the overall evidence for Gq activation, with no specific concerns raised about the DAG/PKC data.

Both support megaplex formation with Gαq/11. OpenEval emphasizes NanoBiT proximity assays and confocal microscopy with V2β2AR as negative control. Peer reviewers acknowledge this 'adds to a growing body of evidence that G proteins and beta-arrestin can associate with GPCR complexes simultaneously,' though the reviewer suggests receptor oligomers as an alternative organizational mechanism.

Both support β-arrestin potentiation of endosomal G protein activation. OpenEval focuses on transduction coefficient analysis comparing V2R and V2β2AR. Peer review accepts this as part of 'significant findings' about megaplexes, though does not specifically evaluate the potentiation mechanism. Peer reviewer's suggestion of receptor oligomers implies alternative interpretations of the data.

Strong agreement on β-arrestin-independent endosomal signaling using Δβarr1/2 knockout cells. OpenEval notes residual endosomal G protein activation and receptor internalization in knockout cells. Peer reviewers acknowledge this as 'significant findings' and note authors 'added significant amounts of new data to address concerns' about methodology, suggesting initial skepticism was resolved.

Both support generalizability claims (C113, C118) about dual pathways extending to other GPCRs. OpenEval notes the conclusion is supported by experimental data but acknowledges speculation in extrapolating from limited examples. Peer review editor states findings have 'theoretical and practical implications [that] extend to other GPCRs,' directly endorsing generalizability.

Both support V2β2AR characterization as appropriate control. OpenEval validates its use showing maintained G protein activation but lacking stable β-arrestin association. Peer review expresses concern about 'sole use of mini-genes' as a weakness, but concludes 'evidence is overall convincing' after authors added new data, resulting in UNCERTAIN rather than full support.

OpenEval supports initial observational evidence for β-arrestin-independent signaling using V2β2AR (C67-C68), noting ~75% of mG clusters without βarr2 colocalization. Peer review's UNCERTAIN evaluation of V2β2AR data (R4) reflects concerns about minigene constructs, which indirectly affects confidence in these observations despite later confirmation in knockout cells.

Both express uncertainty about mechanistic model for β-arrestin potentiation (C101-C105). OpenEval notes C104-C105 are speculative and cryo-EM structure shows no direct Gs-βarr1 interaction. Peer review also rates this UNCERTAIN, with reviewer suggesting 'receptor oligomers are a more obvious way' for megacomplex organization, implying the Gβγ scaffolding mechanism lacks direct evidence.

Strong agreement on comparative context showing β-arrestin-independent internalization and endosomal signaling in other receptors (C107-C112). OpenEval notes citations to multiple laboratories strengthen the general mechanism argument. Peer review supports generalizability, with editor noting 'theoretical and practical implications extend to other GPCRs.'

OpenEval supports synthesis of findings into comprehensive model (C119-C122, Figure 5) showing both pathways. Peer review implicitly supports this through acceptance of individual findings, with editor describing 'significant findings' and reviewer acknowledging the study 'adds to growing body of evidence.' The model integrates claims evaluated positively in peer R1.

OpenEval supports prior literature establishing V2R and V2β2AR properties (C47-C49, C51-C52) that justify experimental design. Peer review's UNCERTAIN evaluation reflects concerns about minigene approach despite acknowledging authors 'added significant amounts of new data,' suggesting the cited prior work is accepted but application in current study raises methodological questions.

OpenEval supports claims about V2R's sustained endosomal G protein activation (C3-C5) distinguishing it from canonical GPCR behavior. Peer review implicitly supports this through acceptance of endosomal signaling findings, with reviewer noting the study 'adds to growing body of evidence' about non-canonical GPCR signaling patterns.

OpenEval supports synthesis from Δβarr1/2 experiments and megaplex assays (C115), noting substantial but incomplete reduction of endosomal signaling. Peer review supports related findings about megaplexes and dual pathways, with this synthesis claim falling within the scope of accepted 'significant findings' about simultaneous G protein and β-arrestin association.

OpenEval supports methodological claim (C82) about mG protein recruitment reflecting direct receptor-G protein interaction rather than amplified downstream responses. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; this methodological distinction was not explicitly discussed by reviewers.

OpenEval supports comparative context from PTHR literature (C83-C85) showing V2R represents distinct signaling pattern. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not specifically comment on PTHR comparisons.

OpenEval supports literature context (C86-C89) showing endosomal Gαq/11 signaling occurs in other receptors and selectivity can differ by compartment. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though this context supports generalizability claims that peer reviewers did endorse.

OpenEval supports summary of G protein selectivity mechanisms (C90-C91) at plasma membrane and inference about additional endosomal factors. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not specifically discuss selectivity mechanisms.

OpenEval supports established mechanistic context for V2R as Class B GPCR (C92-C98) with structural and functional distinctions. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; this background context was not explicitly evaluated by reviewers.

OpenEval supports prior literature summary on megaplex composition (C99), establishing novelty of demonstrating Gαq/11 megaplexes. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers accepted megaplex findings without discussing prior literature on composition.

OpenEval supports citation (C106) of prior work using fusion constructs showing β-arrestin binding does not preclude G protein activation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; this supporting literature was not specifically discussed by reviewers.

OpenEval supports extensive background claims (C1, C10-C32) providing established knowledge and appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not systematically evaluate background/introduction claims, focusing instead on novel experimental findings.
